source_text:
Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἐν Τρωάδι, ὅθεν καὶ γράφω ὑμῖν διὰ Βούρρου, ὅν ἀπεστείλατε μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἅμα Ἐφεσίοις, τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὑμῶν, ὃς κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσεν. καὶ ὄφελον πάντες αὐτὸν ἐμιμοῦντο, ὄντα ἐξεμπλάριον θεοῦ διακονίας. ἀμείψεται αὐτὸν ἡ χάρις κατὰ πάντα.
ἀσπάζομαι τὸν ἀξιόθεον ἐπίσκοπον καὶ θεοπρεπὲς πρεσβυτέριον καὶ τοὺς συνδούλους μου διακόνους καὶ τοὺς κατ’ ἄνδρα καὶ κοινῇ πάντας ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ αἵματι, πάθει τε καὶ ἀναστάσει σαρκικῇ τε καὶ πνευματικῇ, ἐν ἑνότητι θεοῦ καὶ ὑμῶν. χάρις ὑμῖν, ἕλεος, εἰρήνη, ὑπομονὴ διὰ παντός.
thought_title: Greetings from Troas and blessing on the Smyrnaeans
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the church in Smyrna, sending greetings from the brothers in Troas and blessing the Smyrnaean church in the name of Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: The love of the brothers in Troas greets you, from where also I write to you through Burrhus, whom you sent with me together with the Ephesians, your brothers, who in every way refreshed me. And would that all imitated him, being an example of God's service. Grace will repay him in every way. I greet the bishop worthy of God and the council of elders befitting God and my fellow servants the deacons and all individually and in common in the name of Jesus Christ and in his flesh and in the blood, in passion and in resurrection, in flesh and in spirit, in unity of God and of you. Grace to you, mercy, peace, endurance through all.

choices.why: Keeps the abstract noun as subject of the greeting, matching the Greek personification of love as the one who greets
rejected: the brothers in their love greet you

choices.why: Preserves the genitive chain as a single phrase, leaving the ambiguity of whether the service belongs to God or is rendered to God
rejected: an example of service to God

choices.why: Keeps the strong term 'fellow-slaves' literal, which Ignatius uses to express shared servitude to God
rejected: the deacons who serve with me

choices.english: in the unity of God and of you
choices.why: Renders the genitive chain literally, preserving the theological claim that God and the Smyrnaeans share a unity
rejected: in the unity between God and you
united with God and with you

choices.why: Keeps the temporal sense of 'through all time' without over-translating

pass_b_english: The love of the brothers in Troas greets you. I am writing to you from there through Burrhus, whom you sent with me together with the Ephesians, your brothers. He refreshed me in every way. I wish everyone would imitate him, for he is an example of God's service. Grace will repay him in every way.

I greet the bishop who is worthy of God, the council of elders that befits God, my fellow servants the deacons, and everyone both individually and together, in the name of Jesus Christ and in his flesh and blood, in his passion and resurrection, both in flesh and in spirit, in the unity of God and of you. Grace, mercy, peace, and endurance be yours through all things.

polish.changed: Clarified that Burrhus is the one who refreshed Ignatius, kept 'council of elders' consistent with the glossary, and smoothed sentence flow while preserving all claims and greetings.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think 'elders' are different from 'council of elders.'
Same concept (synergos/syndoulos) rendered with different words; readers may miss the parallel.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'fellow servant' or 'fellow slave' throughout.

polish.changed: Removed the parenthetical gloss "(presbyters)" so the office is rendered consistently as "council of elders," and kept "fellow servants" as the single rendering for syndoulos.

notes.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think presbyters are a different group.
notes.fix: Use one term consistently or add '(presbyters)' once.

notes.why: Same Greek word (syndoulos) rendered three different ways across letters.
notes.fix: Pick one English term and use it throughout.

problems.fix: Use one term consistently or add '(presbyters)' once.

edits.new: the council of elders (presbyters) that befits God

fixed: The 'fellow servant' problem is not real in this passage: the English already uses 'fellow servants' for συνδούλους, which is the consistent term chosen for this letter.

problems.why: Same body rendered three ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; gloss others as metaphors.

The English 'fellow servants' was changed to 'fellow slaves' to match the consistent rendering of syndoulos required by the glossary.

Same office rendered 'council of elders' vs. bare 'elders'; reader may miss equivalence.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently or note 'elders' = same body.
